title: Investigate a spreading incident
scenario: A hidden fault on one lamp dependency slows or breaks the three-product catalog. Diagnose whether the impact spreads through shared workers or a failed catalog response.
why: The visible victims may be healthy products. Find the cause before choosing a timeout, breaker or fallback.
reproduce: Ask a partner to seed one incident from docs/facilitator.md. Record your diagnosis before inspecting Network Faults.
ready: {{ready}} Record the healthy baseline before your partner seeds the hidden fault. Do not clear it afterward. A second person is required.
assignment: Which lamp dependency failed, how does the impact spread, and what contains it?

tasks.title: Arrange one hidden incident
tasks.instruction: Record a healthy baseline, then ask a partner to seed Assignment 3 without revealing it. Keep traffic fixed and set an abort condition.

tasks.title: Collect the customer symptoms
tasks.instruction: Compare availability and delivery catalogs. Record times, status, chair/desk results, workers, queue and new rejections with timestamps. Leave fault controls closed.

tasks.title: Write a supported diagnosis
tasks.instruction: Use dependency outcomes, latency and worker charts to predict the fault and how it spreads. Record an alternative explanation before opening controls.

tasks.title: Confirm and contain the mechanism
tasks.instruction: Inspect Network Faults with your partner. Keep the original fault. For slow calls, use a short timeout plus fallback/breaker; for a disconnect, preserve honest partial results.

tasks.title: Validate the healthy products and reveal
tasks.instruction: Retest the same views in fresh windows. Compare healthy products, queue, catalog results and missing data. Ask for the reveal and check your diagnosis. {{cleanup}}

done: You recorded a diagnosis and propagation mechanism before inspecting fault controls.
You retested the identical incident and showed which healthy-product or catalog outcome improved, while recording the affected product’s missing data.
You compared the diagnosis with the reveal and restored all three products.
solution: Slow Inventory can delay both catalog views and occupy workers, causing healthy chair/desk requests to wait or fail.
Disconnected lamp Shipping fails delivery aggregation while availability works. Fast failure need not fill the queue.
A timeout bounds waiting; the breaker pauses repeated failures; fallback preserves partial results. Choose from the evidence.
Retest the same fault and traffic. State what improved and what remains missing, then restore all products.

fields.label: Customer symptom and time window
fields.prompt: Which customer view failed or slowed, and when?

fields.label: Grafana evidence
fields.prompt: Which dependency and Grafana signals changed? Name the panels.

fields.label: Hypothesis and uncertainty
fields.prompt: What is the likely fault? What else could explain it?

fields.label: {{mitigationLabel}}
fields.prompt: What did you change, and why? {{mitigationGuidance}}

fields.label: Validation under the same incident
fields.prompt: Compare before and after under the same fault. {{measurementGuidance}}

fields.label: {{conclusionLabel}}
fields.prompt: What did the reveal confirm? What trade-off remains? Confirm cleanup.
